First, we can simplify the limit using trigonometric identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{{\theta }^{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}({\theta }^{2}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{{\theta }^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{{\theta }^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Rewriting the given limit using the algebra of limits and applying our special limit, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{{\theta }^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{({lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{\theta }^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{1}{{({lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta })}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{(1)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =1.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\frac{{\theta }^{2}}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =1\cdot 1=1.\end{aligned}
$$
